channel.title: The ThriveWell Journal
channel.description: Insights from ThriveWell Care Collective on leadership, caregiving, and restorative wellness for women who care for others.

item.title: Making Room for What Matters This Thanksgiving
item.description: Thanksgiving is just a few days away, and for many of us, that means there's a lot happening.

item.title: Making Caregiving Easier Every Day
item.description: When you care for someone else, even ordinary tasks can begin to take more energy than you realize.

item.title: Finding Connection When So Much of Life Is Spent Caring for Others
item.description: I've been thinking lately about the difference between being surrounded by people and feeling connected to them.

item.title: A Day of Connection, Community, and Care at the Cetronia Health & Wellness Expo
item.description: On November 7, 2026, ThriveWell Care Collective™ had the pleasure of participating in the 5th Annual Health & Wellness Expo hosted by Cetronia Ambulance Corps in Allentown, Pennsylvania.

item.title: Caregiver Fatigue: When Caring for Others Leaves You Running on Empty
item.description: Recognizing the signs of exhaustion, understanding why it happens, and finding meaningful ways to care for yourself.

item.title: Caring for Others Without Losing Sight of Our Own Capacity
item.description: Have you ever reached the end of a day and wondered how you managed to get everything done?

item.title: When Did Everything Become My Responsibility?
item.description: Have you ever found yourself lying awake at night thinking about things that aren't entirely yours to figure out?

item.title: Grounding Techniques: Finding Your Way Back to the Present
item.description: Life can feel overwhelming, especially when you're caring for others, managing responsibilities, or navigating a busy day. Sometimes, even a few moments of intentional awareness can help you feel more centered.

item.title: Making Space for Myself: A Personal Reflection on Learning to Pause
item.description: I've spent much of my life in roles that involve caring for, supporting, teaching, and helping others. Whether in my professional work, with family, or in my community, I've often been the person who tries to figure things out, find solutions, and keep things moving forward.

item.title: A Moment for Yourself: Journaling Prompts for Women Who Care
item.description: When was the last time you stopped and asked yourself, "How am I doing?" It's a simple question, but when you're busy taking care of everyone else, it can be surprisingly easy to forget to ask.

item.title: A Little Space for Yourself: Journaling Through the Demands of Caregiving
item.description: When you're busy caring for everyone else, it's easy to forget to check in with yourself. Maybe your day begins with getting the kids ready, checking on a parent, answering work messages, or thinking about everything that needs to get done.

item.title: From Leading Change to Caring for the People Who Carry It
item.description: For much of my career, I have worked in change. I have helped organizations prepare people for new systems, new processes, new ways of working, new expectations, and new realities.
